nodes.label: Hierarchical Namespace Strategy
nodes.rationale: childNamespace = parentNamespace + '.' + parentRecordName.toLowerCase(), so repeated type names (e.g. Address) at different hierarchy positions get unique full names and never collide.

nodes.label: Numeric/Date-to-String Mapping Rationale
nodes.rationale: All numeric and date/time OpenAPI types are intentionally mapped to Avro string to avoid precision loss and simplify cross-system compatibility.

nodes.label: can't redefine Compile Error Behaviour
nodes.rationale: Avro's Maven plugin compiles .avsc files independently; two files defining the same full type name fail with can't redefine. Hierarchical namespacing prevents this by guaranteeing unique full names.

nodes.label: Numeric/Date-to-String Mapping Rationale (README)
nodes.rationale: Numeric and date/time types are deliberately mapped to string to avoid precision loss and ease cross-system compatibility; explicitly stated as an intentional design choice, not a bug.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Namespace Strategy (README)
nodes.rationale: Each named type gets a namespace encoding its position in the schema tree (parentNamespace.parentRecordName) so repeated type names like Address stay unique and mvn compile never hits can't redefine.
